Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 35-year-old male with new-onset episodic frontal headaches, palpitations, heat intolerance, SOB, bilateral arm paresthesias, weight loss, and low libido beginning after a job change. History of thyroid disease on thyroxine replacement.

Working diagnosis: 1) Suspected iatrogenic hyperthyroidism (over-replacement) versus endogenous hyperthyroidism. 2) Occupational stress/anxiety with tension-type headaches also possible contributor.

Differential diagnoses consistent with transcript and DDx:  
• Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism due to excessive thyroxine – High likelihood given classic hyper-thyroid symptoms and current thyroxine therapy.  
• Stress-related/anxiety or panic disorder with tension headaches – Moderate likelihood; temporal link to work stress; autonomic symptoms may be anxiety-mediated.  
• Primary tension or migraine headaches – Moderate likelihood for headache component but does not explain systemic symptoms.

Management Plan

- Arrange in-person clinic appointment for full physical examination (vitals, cardiovascular, respiratory, neurological).  
- Order blood tests: Thyroid function (TSH, free T4, free T3), full blood count, electrolytes, fasting glucose, lipids; consider B12 and iron studies given paresthesias and weight loss.  
- Review current thyroxine dose and adherence; withhold or adjust pending TFT results if indicated.  
- Provide education on stress management; discuss workplace ergonomics and regular breaks from screen.  
- No new medications initiated pending evaluation.  
- Advise patient to seek urgent care if palpitations become prolonged, severe SOB, or neurological deficits develop.  
- Follow-up: Booked via app; results review and management within one week after labs.

Consider:

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits): Not recorded  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral: Not recorded  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support): To be considered after assessment of anxiety/stress levels  
- CTG registration: Not recorded  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test): Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Iatrogenic hyperthyroidism – High likelihood  
   Justification: On thyroxine; heat intolerance, weight loss, palpitations, decreased libido and anxiety-like symptoms match hyper-thyroid excess.

2. Stress-related/anxiety or panic disorder with tension headaches – Moderate likelihood  
   Justification: Symptoms predominantly at work; high perceived stress; autonomic manifestations can mimic hyper-thyroid symptoms.

3. Primary tension or migraine headache – Moderate likelihood  
   Justification: Frontal severe headaches triggered by computer use; mild nausea supportive of migraine component.

Quality checks

● Missing but expected: Vital signs, BMI, cardiovascular and neurological exam, immunisation status, detailed mental health screening, family history, hearing and vision screening, alcohol units per week, sleep assessment.  
● No direct contradictions between transcript and DDx noted.  
● Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses/unfinished sentences but clinical content understandable.
